note:
ALA-LC Shan Romanization Table, 2012 version (no earlier versions), pp. 1-5; held source interscript-private-references/alalc/alalc-shan.pdf (sha256 f5bae16143ba557ff1af6296c7c742a7c3709fab9731a3dd7694a95ffab9d715; the duplicate alalc-shan.pdf.pdf is byte-identical). Extraction: the PDF text layer is real Unicode for the vowel table, the finals/tone/punctuation rows, the numerals, the abbreviations, the notes and all 15 sample romanizations (Word PDFMaker; Cordia/Times/ArialUnicode); the 33 consonant vernacular cells extract only as shape-font ASCII lookalikes (u c U C i q ! Q @ n # $ % ...), while the xa and fa cells render and extract as REAL Shan glyphs - the print's own codepoint anchors. Every printed row was cross-checked against rendered page images (300 dpi pages, 600-900 dpi cell crops).
Consonant identification (the lao #326 bitmap-ID class, weaker here - the lookalike glyphs carry no shape information): the 33 lookalike cells are identified from (a) the corpus's own generation record for this exact document (tools/gen-shan.py), (b) Shan alphabet-order coherence, and (c) three independent anchor sets - the print's two real-glyph cells and the document's own sample vocabulary, whose Shan letters appear with the print's romanizations (papʻ pū″ puinʻ anchor ပ=p; naunʻ″ anchors ၼ=n; phanʻ/phāi̢ anchor ၽ=ph). ANCHOR CORRECTIONS to the map's keys (gen-shan keys the na/pha/xa/fa rows to letters the document does not use): the xa row = ႀ U+1080 (SHAN THA; real-glyph anchor; the map keys ႀ -> tha), the fa row = ၾ U+107E (SHAN FA; real-glyph anchor; the map keys ၾ -> xa and keys fa to ႎ U+108E MYANMAR LETTER RUMAI PALAUNG FA, a letter absent from the document), the na row = ၼ U+107C SHAN NA (text anchor; map keys န U+1014), the pha row = ၽ U+107D SHAN PHA (text anchor; map keys ဖ U+1016). The tha row's vernacular cell carries no readable codepoint; gen-shan's key (ႀ) is disproven by the xa anchor - the alphabet-position inference ထ U+1011 is recorded as an UNCERTAIN identification (lao precedent) and excluded from the generated tests. The ʼa row's value prints U+2019; the map uses the apostrophe U+02BC - map form kept, lookalike divergence recorded (bod F12 class). The row-4 and row-5 variant cells print two GLYPH-IDENTICAL forms in the print itself (font collapse; both extract U+102F / U+1030) - transcribed once each.
Testing frame (the tha #331 convention): consonant rows tested in their ႃ-frame composition (C + ႃ = the printed initial value + the printed aa row 1: ၶႃ -> khā tests kha's kh); the bare single-letter readings are checked separately and are findings (inherent-a class). Vowel rows tested in ၵ-carrier compositions. The iscrs runtime (interscript-rs 0.2.x) classified every candidate row; every generated row's value is the printed value composed per the table, verified byte-identical at runtime.
Findings (map-vs-source; transcribed rows EXCLUDED from the generated tests, never forced green; record for the maps-fix pipeline; page anchors to the 2012 print):
1. XA/FA TRANSPOSITION (MAJOR, p. 1 rows xa/fa): the map keys ႀ -> tha and ၾ -> xa and fa -> ႎ; the print anchors ႀ = xa and ၾ = fa. Runtime: ႀႃ -> thā (print xā), ၾႃ -> xā (print fā); the map's ႎ -> fa rule is unreachable (ႎ appears nowhere in the document).
2. THA ROW UNENCODED (p. 1 row 17): with gen-shan's ႀ key disproven, the tha row's true codepoint is unestablished; the alphabet-position inference ထ (U+1011) has no map rule (ထႃ -> ထā leak). Uncertain identification, excluded.
3. NA/PHA KEYS (p. 1 rows na/pha): the document's own text uses ၼ (U+107C) and ၽ (U+107D) for n/ph (naunʻ″, phanʻ, phāi̢); the map keys na -> န and pha -> ဖ, so ၼႃ -> ၼā and ၽႃ -> ၽā leak (print nā/phā) and the map's န/ဖ rules are unreachable keys.
4. INHERENT-A (Note 2, p. 2 - documented design): the print romanizes every bare consonant WITH the inherent a (ka kha ga ...); the map's bare rules emit the initial value only (ၵ -> k). All 34 bare consonant readings fail (the ʼa row passes via the map's own bare-ʼa rule). The map description states "Consonants carry the inherent vowel a (per Note 2)" but no rule realizes it - stale-note class (lao #326 F9).
5. SYLLABLE-FINAL ASAT DELETED (MAJOR, p. 3 finals row 1): the print romanizes the asat ် (U+103A) as ʻ (U+02BB, "(ayn)"); the map DELETES it (sub "်" ""): ၵ် -> k (print kʻ). Every one of the 15 sample romanizations carries the final ʻ (cavʻ sukʻ sīla khanʻʺ), so the deletion breaks the whole sample section.
6. ANUSVARA UNENCODED (p. 3 finals row 2): ံ (U+1036) -> ṃ (U+1E43) has no map rule; ၵံ -> ၵံ leak (print kṃ). The print's own sample caṃ″ (ၼင်းၸံး) needs it.
7. AAI GRID OFF-BY-ONE SIGN (MAJOR, p. 2 row 12): the printed ႆ + ႃ / ႆ + ၢ forms (U+1086, the vowel-marking sign of rows 11/12/14) -> āi are UNENCODED: ၵႆႃ -> kaiႃ, ၵႆၢ -> kaiၢ (the ႆ is consumed by the ai rule, the aa leaks). The map's āi grids key the TONE-2 sign ႇ (U+1087) instead (ၵႇႃ -> kāi) - a form the vowel table never prints; the map description's "the tone-sign combinations ႆ act as vowel markers" names the right sign but the emitted grids use ႇ.
8. U+1062 SECOND-AA FORM UNENCODED (p. 1 row 1 form 2): ၢ (U+1062) -> ā has no map rule (ၵၢ -> ၵၢ leak). The sign is live in the document's own text (ၸၢတ်ႈ cātʻ, ၽႆၢႇ phāi̢).
9. ROW 7 FORMS 2-3 UNENCODED (p. 2): ႅ (U+1085 SHAN E ABOVE; ၵႅ -> leak) and the ေ◌ေ◌◌ double-e form (ေၵေၵ -> keke leak); only the ႄ (U+1084) preposed form composes (ႄၵ -> kè).
10. PREPOSED ြ MEDIAL (p. 2 medials row 2): the print's ြ◌◌ form composes the medial r inside the onset (ြၽႃး -> phrā″); the map's standalone ြ -> r rule yields ြၵ -> rk. The postposed medials ျ -> ky and ႂ -> kv pass.
11. TONE MARKS LEAK (p. 3 tone table, 5 rows): ႇ ႈ း Ⴍ ႊ have no rules and pass through (ၵႇ -> ၵႇ, ၵႈ, ၵး, ၵྌ, ၵႊ); the print gives ̢ (U+0322 right hook), ̐ (U+0310 candrabindu), ″ (U+2033 double prime), ´ (U+00B4 prime), ˝ (U+02DD double acute) - e.g. ၵႇ -> ၵႇ (print k̢). The map's note claims "Tone signs 2-6 (U+1087 ff.) ... are not romanized" but encodes no deletions - stale note (lao #326 F9 class), and the print's own values are the marks, not silence.
12. PUNCTUATION UNENCODED (p. 3): ၊ (U+104A) -> comma and ။ (U+104B) -> period have no rules; both leak.
13. DIGITS KEY THE WRONG SCRIPT (MAJOR, p. 3-4 numerals): the map's 0-9 rules key the LIMBU digits U+1946-194F (᥆-᥏); the print's Shan digits ႐-႙ (U+1090-1099) and Burmese alternates ၀-၉ (U+1040-1049) all leak (႐ -> ႐, print 0). The Limbu keys are unreachable - no Limbu digit can appear in Shan text.
14. ABBREVIATIONS UNENCODED (p. 4): ႟ (U+109F) -> u* and ႞ (U+109E SHAN ONE) -> n* have no rules; both leak.
15. SAMPLE ROMANIZATIONS (pp. 4-5, 15 words): not reproducible as a class - the final-asat deletion (finding 5), the tone leaks (11), the anusvara (6) and the ၼ ၽ keys (3) break them (e.g. မွင်း -> mauṅး vs print mauṅʻʺ; ၽႆၢႇ -> ၽႆၢႇ vs print phāi̢; တႆး -> taiး vs print Taiʺ). Word Division is caller-level (space after each syllable).
16. MAP-ONLY RULES (no printed row): the ႇ-keyed aa/vowel grids (finding 7), the bare aa signs ာ U+102C and ါ U+102B (the hand test's ၵါ keys U+102B TALL AA - a form the vowel table does not print; the table's aa forms are ႃ and ၢ), န (U+1014), ဖ (U+1016) and ႎ (U+108E) consonant keys (findings 1, 3).
Bookkeeping: 91 table rows transcribed and checked (35 consonant rows: 30 generated via their ႃ-frames incl. the map-form ʼa reading, 5 excluded; 25 vowel forms incl. 2 glyph-identical duplicate variants transcribed once: 17 generated, 5 excluded, the aa-sign forms counted with their rows; 3 medials: 2 generated, 1 excluded; 2 finals, 5 tone rows, 2 punctuation rows, 20 numerals, 2 abbreviations: all excluded) - the rows array carries the 49 generated rows exactly; 42 printed rows are the findings above, excluded from generation; the 34 bare consonant readings that fail the inherent-a check are findings recorded on the generated rows' account; the 15 sample words are checked as a class (finding 15). Regenerating via scripts/gen-row-tests.mjs from this artifact reproduces the embedded block byte-for-byte.
